summary: A firstborn son can be a bechor for getting a double share of the inheritance, for pidyon haben with a Kohen, for both, or for neither. The mishnah gives examples of each.

chunks.he: יֵשׁ בְּכוֹר לַנַּחֲלָה וְאֵינוֹ בְכוֹר לַכֹּהֵן,
chunks.en: Some are a bechor for inheritance but not a bechor for the Kohen,
chunks.st: There is a son who is a firstborn with regard to inheritance but is not a firstborn with regard to the requirement of redemption from a priest.

chunks.en: some are a bechor for the Kohen but not for inheritance,
chunks.st: There is another who is a firstborn with regard to redemption from a priest but is not a firstborn with regard to inheritance.

chunks.en: some are a bechor for inheritance and for the Kohen,
chunks.st: There is another who is a firstborn with regard to inheritance and with regard to redemption from a priest.

chunks.he: יֵשׁ שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְכוֹר לֹא לַנַּחֲלָה וְלֹא לַכֹּהֵן.
chunks.en: and some are not a bechor, not for inheritance and not for the Kohen.
chunks.st: And there is another who is not a firstborn at all, neither with regard to inheritance nor with regard to redemption from a priest.

chunks.he: אֵיזֶהוּ בְּכוֹר לַנַּחֲלָה וְאֵינוֹ בְכוֹר לַכֹּהֵן,

chunks.he: הַבָּא אַחַר הַנְּפָלִים שֶׁיָּצָא רֹאשׁוֹ חַי,
chunks.en: One born after an earlier baby that did not live, even if it came out alive at first,
chunks.st: It is a son who came after miscarriage of an underdeveloped fetus, even where the head of the underdeveloped fetus emerged alive;

chunks.en: or after a full-term baby that did not live,

chunks.en: or after a birth that looked like an animal or a bird.
chunks.st: The same applies to a son born to a woman who had previously miscarried a fetus that had the appearance of a type of domesticated animal, undomesticated animal, or bird,
chunks.stMore: as that is considered the opening of the womb. This is

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: only if it had the shape of a person.
chunks.st: unless his birth follows the birth of an animal that takes the form of a person.

chunks.en: A woman who lost an unformed baby or a birth sac,
chunks.st: In the case of a woman who miscarries a fetus in the form of a sandal fish or from whom an afterbirth

chunks.en: or a sac with a forming baby, or one that came out in parts:

chunks.st: that son is a firstborn with regard to inheritance but is not a firstborn with regard to redemption from a priest.

summary: A baby born through a cut in his mother's side, and the one born after him: Rabbi Shimon says each one counts as a bechor in a different way.

chunks.en: A baby born through his mother's side, and the one born after him:
chunks.st: In the case of a boy born by caesarean section and the son who follows him,

chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: If one of them died within thirty days,
chunks.st: If one of them dies within thirty days
chunks.stMore: of birth, before the obligation to redeem the firstborn takes effect,

summary: The money the Torah sets for pidyon haben and for some other payments is counted in holy shekels, using the coins of Tzor.

chunks.en: The five sela'im for a son

chunks.stMore: with regard to which it is written: “Five shekels of silver, after the shekel of the Sanctuary” (Numbers 18:16),

chunks.en: are in the coins of Tzor.
chunks.st: are calculated using a Tyrian maneh.
chunks.stMore: The silver content of the Tyrian coinage is significantly higher than that of provincial coinage, which is worth one-eighth its value.

words.note: Tzor's silver coins were pure and heavy.

chunks.en: The thirty paid for a slave,

chunks.en: in the coins of Tzor.

chunks.he: חַיָּב לִתֵּן לוֹ וּבְנוֹ אֵינוֹ פָדוּי,
chunks.en: he must give it to him, but his son is not redeemed.
chunks.st: the father is obligated to give them to him but his son is not redeemed.

chunks.en: So if the Kohen wants
chunks.st: Therefore, if the priest wished to give back the five sela coins

chunks.en: to give it back to him as a present, he may.
chunks.st: to him as a gift he is permitted to do so.

chunks.en: Someone who set aside money to redeem his son, and lost it,
chunks.st: With regard to one who designates five sela coins for redemption of his firstborn son and he lost the coins before he gave them to the priest,

chunks.en: is responsible for it,
chunks.st: the father bears financial responsibility for their loss,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says,
chunks.st: as it is stated
chunks.stMore: to Aaron the priest: “Everything that opens the womb in man and animal

chunks.en: "It shall be yours, and you shall surely redeem."
chunks.st: shall be yours”; and only afterward it says: “You shall redeem
chunks.stMore: the firstborn of man” (Numbers 18:15). This indicates that only after the money shall be in the possession of the priest is the son redeemed.

summary: A bechor gets a double share of his father's property. The mishnah teaches which kinds of property he does not get double from.

chunks.he: הַבְּכוֹר נוֹטֵל פִּי שְׁנַיִם בְּנִכְסֵי הָאָב,
chunks.en: A bechor takes a double share of his father's property,
chunks.st: The firstborn son takes a double portion, i.e., twice the portion taken by the other sons, when inheriting the property of the father,

chunks.he: וְאֵינוֹ נוֹטֵל פִּי שְׁנַיִם בְּנִכְסֵי הָאֵם.
chunks.en: but he does not take a double share of his mother's property.
chunks.st: but he does not take twice the portion when inheriting the property of the mother.

chunks.en: And he does not take a double share of the growth in value,
chunks.st: And neither does he take twice the portion in any enhancement
chunks.stMore: of the value of the property after the death of the father,

chunks.en: or of what was owed to his father, like what he had.
chunks.st: nor does he take twice the portion in property due the father, as he does in property the father possessed.

chunks.en: And a woman does not, for her kesubah,
chunks.st: And neither does a woman take these portions, i.e., any enhancement of the value of the property or the property due the husband, from her husband’s property for payment of her marriage contract upon her divorce or her husband’s death;

chunks.en: nor the daughters for their food,
chunks.st: nor do the daughters take this share of the property for their sustenance,
chunks.stMore: to which they are entitled from their late father’s possessions.

chunks.en: nor the yavam.
chunks.st: Nor does a man whose married brother died childless [yavam]
chunks.stMore: receive these portions, even though he acquires his brother’s portion of their shared father’s inheritance after performing levirate marriage with his brother’s wife.

words.note: The brother who marries his brother's widow.

chunks.en: None of them take from the growth in value,
chunks.st: The mishna summarizes: And all of them do not take a portion in any enhancement
chunks.stMore: of the value of the property after the death of the owner,

chunks.en: or from what was owed, like what was held.
chunks.st: nor do they take a portion in property due the deceased, as they do in property in his possession.

summary: Which fields do not go back to their first owners in the Yovel year, and the Rabbis' argument about a gift.

chunks.en: These do not go back in the Yovel:
chunks.st: And these are the people whose properties, unlike an ancestral field, do not return to their original owners in the Jubilee
chunks.stMore: Year: The firstborn who inherited his father’s property by the right of

words.note: The fiftieth year, when fields go back to their first owners.

chunks.en: the bechor's extra share, and one who inherits from his wife,
chunks.st: primogeniture need not return the extra portion for redistribution among the brothers; and one who inherits his wife’s property need not return it to her family;

chunks.en: and one who does yibum with his brother's widow,
chunks.st: and one who consummates the levirate marriage with the wife of his brother
chunks.stMore: and gains the right to his brother’s property need not return it for redistribution among the brothers.

words.en: and the one who does yibum

chunks.en: and a gift. That is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: And likewise, a gift of land need not be returned to the original owners in the Jubilee Year; this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: a gift is like a sale.
chunks.st: The halakhic status of a gift is like that of a sale, and it must be returned.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar says:

chunks.en: they all go back in the Yovel.
chunks.st: All these lands return in the Jubilee Year.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka says:

chunks.en: one who inherits from his wife
chunks.st: Even one who inherits his wife’s property

chunks.en: must give it back to her family, and take off
chunks.st: must return the land to the members of her father’s family and should deduct

chunks.en: some money from them.
chunks.st: from them the monetary
